These appeals coming on for admission this day, the cou  following:
 ORDER

These miscellaneous appeals have been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved with the award dated 01.04.2015 passed by 9th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur in MVC Nos.187/2012 and 186/2012 respectively.

entities.text: 9th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Both the appeals are arises from the same incident and the same award.

2. In a nutshell, the facts giving rise of the case are that on 02.02.2012, appellant Bedilal on his motorcycle along with claimant Imratlal was returning to his home and when they reached near Hanuman Mandir then the driver of the offending tractor driving rashly and negligently hit the motorcycle driven by Bedilal and both suffered injuries.
Report was lodged at Police Station Bhedaghat.
The appellants were medically examined.
Appellant Bedilal was admitted in Apex Hospital, Jabalpur from 02.02.2012 to 07.02.2012 and the appellant Imratlal was admitted in the same hospital on 02.02.2012 and discharged on 03.02.2012.

3. Before the Claim Tribunal the respondents filed their reply and after hearing the parties the Claim Tribunal by the impugned award has held the appellant Bedilal for the contributory negligence and reduced the compensation amount 50% and also awarded the claim of Imratlal.

4. In MA No.1411 of 2015, appellant Imratlal has challenged the award stating that Claim Tribunal has illegally awarded a meager amount and Claim Tribunal has not properly appreciated the fact that the appellant has sustained grievous injuries and fracture on nose and disfigurement.

The Claim Tribunal has wrongly assessed that the offending vehicle was driven on the breach of the policy and held liable the appellants for the contributory negligence and prayed for enhancement and has submitted that impugned award be set aside and liability be fastened on the Insurance Company.

5. In MA No.1410 of 2015, appellant Bedilal has also challenged the award on the ground that the appellant suffered the grievous injuries, fracture and disfigurement but Claim Tribunal has awarded Bedilal vs Sriram Patel on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145411458/
2 less amount in ratio to injury suffered by him.
The Claim Tribunal has not awarded the sufficient amount in the medical expenses and transportation.
He further submitted that the Claim Tribunal has wrongly exonerated the Insurance Company and held liable the appellant for contributory negligence.

6. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 has submitted that in these appeals the Insurance Company cannot be held liable as at the time of incident, the tractor was insured for the agricultural purpose only and at the time of incident the tractor was engaged under contract carrying the luggage and electric items of Madhya Pradesh Electricity Board which is a clear violation of the policy.

He has further submitted that the incident has occurred in the mid of the road and head on collusion had taken place and Bedilal himself has admitted that the incident has taken as head on collusion and if he was conscious, the incident would have been averted.
7. I have heard the parties and perused the records.

8. On the point of contributory negligence, the driver of the motorcycle appellant Bedilal in para-5 of the cross examination has admitted that he was returning to his Village Garhpipariya and offending tractor was coming toward the Sahpura side and collusion has taken place.
He has also admitted that as per the claim, the head on collusion has taken place.
He has also admitted that if both the driver were vigilant, the accident would not had happened.
He also admitted that he himself was driving the motorcycle.
9. In this case also the claimant has filed the FIR and medical documents but has not filed the spot map.
In this situation when the head on collusion has taken place and driver of the motorcycle himself admitted that the he would have been vigilant enough, the incident would have been averted.
It is clear cut case of contributory negligence.

10. Before the Claim Tribunal the Insurance Company has examined Vishwanath Das (NAW-2) and in his statement he has clearly stated that the offending tractor No.MP-21-C-9411 was insured with National Insurance Company and as per the terms and conditions of the policy (Ex.D-2), it was prohibited to operate the vehicle on hire and award as the vehicle was insured for the agricultural purpose only and on the date of incident, the vehicle was attached with MPEB on rent and the vehicle was being operated against the conditions of the policy and on that the Insurance Company is not liable.

11. On this point the Claim Tribunal has considered and exonerated the Insurance Company and the Claim Tribunal in its judgment in deciding the issue No.3 has elaborately discussed the fact and legal position and after the analysis it cannot be said that the finding are against the fact or against the law.
12. Regarding Bedilal the Claim Tribunal has considered the medical expenses Rs.21.900/- and awarded Rs.5000/- on the pain and suffering.
Rs.5000/- on the head of attendant, charges and special diet and working loss of one month Rs.4000/- has been calculated.

Bedilal vs Sriram Patel on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145411458/
3
13. On this point as per minimum wages payable to unskilled labourer was Rs.4545/- and the Claim Tribunal has assessed the amount near about that, hence, no substantial difference is found.

On the same way Claim Tribunal has awarded Imratlal, his medical expenses and Rs.2000/- awarded for mental pain and suffering and Rs.2000/- awarded for attendant charges, special diet as he was hospitalized for a day only.

For working loss of 15 days, the Claim Tribunal has awarded Rs.2000/-
and that cannot be said to be lower side, hence, the Claim Tribunal has rightly assessed the loss.

14. Thus, from the above discussion no perversity is found and the Claim Tribunal as properly assessed the loss, hence, appeal being devoid of merit and is hereby dismissed.
15.
Parties shall bear their own cost.
16.With the copy of this order, record of the Claims Tribunal be returned back.
17. Record of the appeal be consigned to record room.
18. Copy of this order be kept in other connected matter.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE DPS Bedilal vs Sriram Patel on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145411458/
